fullPassage:
Even outdoors, although climate (including temperature) is usually regarded as beyond the control of man, localized temperature control is sometimes effective on a microclimate scale. Vancouver, Canada, is a few miles north of the 49th parallel, about 60 miles farther north than Minot, North Dakota, with its legendary harsh winter temperatures. But constant foehn winds off the Pacific Ocean make Vancouver winters mild and wet, although sunshine is scant. When I had a garden there in the late 1940s, a neighbor used to say that I "cheated God" to bring in my lettuce and tomatoes earlier than anyone else. The bed in which the vegetables grew was banked toward the south at approximately 50 degrees, and the area between the plants was covered with flat stones, gathered from the nearby beach, to maximize soil heating from the weak late winter–early spring sun.

Energy can always be injected into an organization to motivate people to do things. Bonuses, promotions, other carrots, and even a few sticks can get people to work harder, for sure, but the gains are, like all manipulations, short-term. Over time, such tactics cost more money and increase stress for employee and employer alike, and eventually will become the main reason people show up for work every day. That's not loyalty. That's the employee version of repeat business. Loyalty among employees is when they turn down more money or benefits to continue working at the same company. Loyalty to a company trumps pay and benefits. And unless you're an astronaut, it's not the work we do that inspires us either. It's the cause that we come to work for. We don't want to come to work to build a wall; we want to come to work to build a cathedral.

In the early 1960s the great American writer James Baldwin wrote: "People are trapped in history, and history is trapped in them." He was speaking to race when he penned those words. But the statement is equally true if the word "people" is replaced with "all of life on Earth, present and past," for each strand of DNA, in each of our cells, is an ancient record of biological history, written in simple code and passed down from generation to generation. One could say that DNA is nothing but history, one with a physical manifestation that was slowly blended and accumulated over countless eons by the most pitiless of all phenomena — natural selection. DNA is a history that is inside us — and yet one that is our master as well, the blueprint for our bodies, and dictator of what we will pass on to our children, gifts that can be blessings — or deadly time bombs. We are indeed trapped in this particular vehicle of history as much as it is trapped in us.

People may not think critically for a variety of reasons, such as laziness and inability, but fear is a big one. Why is that? People don't want to think not just because it's hard, but also because they're afraid it will make them question their long-held beliefs. Your students most likely do want to think about things that can be very controversial, like politics, ethics, and philosophy. But probe even deeper. Once we start thinking deeply, long-held assumptions are challenged. Thought makes us worry that we'll lose our balance and have to look at the world in a different way. We worry about thinking because we care about what we and other people think. Even the most far-fetched ideas have an effect on the world. Non-Euclidean geometry and symbolic logic are about as abstract as thinking can get, but you can't understand Einsteinian gravity without the first and run computers without the second. Thinking is important to us, to others, and to the world we live in. This is one reason why we are so afraid of it: it shakes us to the core.

Digital platforms have made a lot of work less sticky. As work becomes ever more modularised, commoditised and standardised, and as markets for digital work are created, ties between service work and particular places can be disconnected. While the business process of outsourcing that emerged in the 1990s allowed large companies to take advantage of a 'global reserve army' by moving their call centres to cheap and distant labour markets, cloudwork changes the volume and granularity at which geographically non-proximate work can take place. A small business in New York can hire a freelance transcriber in Nairobi one day and New Delhi the next. No offices or factories need to be built, no local regulations are observed, and — in most cases — no local taxes are paid. The switch in the production network of work happens by simply sending some emails or clicking some buttons on a digital work platform. And, in this way, the employer leaves behind no material traces in the places where it was once an employer.

questions.passage: "Where could it be?" Sophie asked herself. It had been more than ten years since she had last visited the area where she had grown up. The village had changed a lot over time. ① Uncertain, she awkwardly looked around at her surroundings. She walked the narrow streets of the village, unsure about which way to go. ② Suddenly, Sophie saw a familiar sight. "Yes, this must be it," she thought. ③ Although the colors were now faded, the familiar shapes on the wall were the same ones she had painted with her father as a child. ④ Sophie nodded, smiled brightly, and walked toward the gate.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
In front of her was a wall with flowers painted on it.

det.korean: "Yes, this must be it"이라고 생각한 직후, 그녀 앞에 꽃이 그려진 벽이 있었다는 문장이 와야 자연스러움. 그 다음 벽의 색이 바랜 것을 설명.
det.analysis:
✅③: "this must be it" 직후 → 꽃 벽 발견 → 색이 바랜 설명으로 연결
❌①: 아직 길을 찾는 중
❌②: 익숙한 광경을 보기 전
❌④: 이미 벽 설명 완료 후
det.tip: 대명사 "this must be it"이 가리키는 대상이 바로 뒤에 나와야 자연스러움

questions.passage: The organ, his most precious possession, was a source of comfort and joy, especially in these uncertain times. ① But his peace was interrupted by the distant roar of engines breaking the calm. ② Francis' heart raced; it was wartime, and soldiers often took what they wanted. ③ Whispering urgently to his sister, Ellen, he led her to hide behind a tall tree, its thick trunk shielding them. ④ Peeking out, Francis stepped outside carefully and looked at the soldiers walking toward their home.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

det.korean: 엔진 소리가 평화를 깨뜨린 직후, 군인들이 나타나는 것이 자연스러움. 그 후 Francis의 심장이 빨리 뛰는 것으로 연결.
det.analysis:
✅②: 엔진 소리 → 군인 등장 → 심장이 뛰는 반응
❌①: 아직 평화가 깨지기 전
❌③: 이미 숨으려고 행동 중
❌④: 이미 밖으로 나와서 보는 중
det.tip: 사건 순서: 엔진 소리 → 군인 등장 → 공포 반응 → 숨기

questions.stem:
주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
down / my / on / pressing / mind

det.korean: press down on(~을 짓누르다) + my mind → "마음을 짓누르는" 비유 표현
det.analysis: pressing down on my mind: press down on(~을 짓누르다) + my mind(내 마음)
det.tip: press down on = ~을 짓누르다 / 무거운 돌이 마음을 짓누르는 비유

questions.passage: After a few nights, we ①<u>ventured</u> out on a hike to 16,000 feet. The group members were all ②<u>experienced</u>, so I couldn't understand why they were climbing so slowly. Having ③<u>trained</u> hard for this, I was in the best shape of my life. Then, as we ④<u>approached</u> 16,000 feet, I suddenly began to feel dizzy. Not long after, I was staggering. In a matter of minutes, I became a basket case, needing assistance just ⑤<u>walk</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: "needing assistance just to walk"에서 '걷기 위해'라는 목적의 to부정사가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
❌⑤walk: needing assistance just to walk → to부정사 필요
✅①ventured: 과거시제 동사
✅②experienced: 형용사(경험 많은)
✅③trained: 분사구문(Having trained)
✅④approached: 과거시제 동사
det.tip: need assistance to V = ~하기 위해 도움이 필요하다

questions.passage: Vera ①<u>couldn't</u> wait for her car to get fixed, but that was going to require longer than initially expected. Unfortunately, that meant ②<u>relying</u> on the bus for her commute. It was already past 7 PM when she stepped off the bus, cold and soaked to the bone, ③<u>having left</u> her umbrella at the gym. Her legs moved on their own, and suddenly, the Cups & Blossoms' bell was ④<u>ringing</u> above her head. She was also polite enough not to ask why Vera looked so tired, which was ⑤<u>appreciating</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: "which was appreciated"에서 주어(it)가 감사히 여겨지는 대상이므로 수동태(was appreciated)가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
❌⑤appreciating: which was appreciated → 수동태 필요
✅①couldn't: 조동사 부정
✅②relying: mean + ~ing(~을 의미하다)
✅③having left: 완료 분사구문
✅④ringing: 진행형(was ringing)
det.tip: which was appreciated = 그것은 감사히 여겨졌다 (수동태)

questions.passage: It was the day I had been ①<u>preparing</u> for. I drove for an hour and a half to apply for a visa. That same day, I helped three people who didn't know English by ②<u>translating</u> for the immigration officer. Believing things were going ③<u>smoothly</u>, I made my way to the counter. Unfortunately, the officer, who had smiled when I was helping her, suddenly turned ④<u>serious</u>. I didn't expect to hear her words of ⑤<u>acceptance</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 빨간 도장, 서류 무시 등 거절 상황이므로 rejection(거절)이 적절. acceptance(수락)는 맥락에 맞지 않음.
det.analysis:
❌⑤acceptance(수락): 원문은 rejection(거절). 빨간 도장+서류 무시=거절 상황
✅①preparing ✅②translating ✅③smoothly ✅④serious

questions.passage: The group members were all ①<u>experienced</u>, so I couldn't understand why they were climbing so slowly — what I thought was a ②<u>ridiculous</u> pace. And, being the rookie, I wanted to prove myself to the group. Why not show off my ③<u>superior</u> conditioning? In a matter of minutes, I became a basket case, needing ④<u>assistance</u> just to walk. Now all I felt was ⑤<u>reward</u> for becoming a burden to the group.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 짐이 된 것에 대해 죄책감(guilt)을 느끼는 것이 자연스러움. reward(보상)는 맥락에 맞지 않음.
det.analysis:
❌⑤reward(보상): 원문은 guilt(죄책감). 짐이 된 것에 보상을 느끼는 것은 부적절
✅①experienced ✅②ridiculous ✅③superior ✅④assistance

questions.passage: Francis Pohan sat at the organ in his Borneo home, a smile on his face as the hymn he had practiced for weeks flowed smoothly under his fingers. The melody blended with the soft sounds of the jungle, filling him with happiness. The organ, his most precious __________, was a source of comfort and joy, especially in these uncertain times.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 가장 소중한 소유물(possession). 오르간은 악기이지만 여기서는 "가장 소중한 소유물"로서 위안과 기쁨의 원천으로 표현됨.
det.analysis:
✅③possession(소유물): 가장 소중한 소유물
❌①instrument(악기): 의미는 통하나 precious와의 조합이 부자연스러움
❌②decoration(장식): 오르간은 장식이 아님
❌④weapon(무기): 문맥과 무관
❌⑤melody(멜로디): 오르간 자체가 멜로디는 아님
det.tip: possession = 소유물 / precious possession = 소중한 소유물

questions.passage: Vera couldn't wait for her car to get fixed, but that was going to require longer than initially expected. Unfortunately, that meant relying on the bus for her __________.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 차가 수리 중이라 버스로 통근(commute)해야 했다.
det.analysis:
✅③commute(통근): 차 수리 중 → 버스로 통근

❌②exercise(운동): 버스를 운동에 이용하지 않음
❌④entertainment(오락): 문맥과 무관
❌⑤hobby(취미): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: commute = 통근 / 차가 고장 → 버스로 통근

Once we start thinking deeply, long-held assumptions are challenged. Thought makes us worry that we'll lose our balance and have to look at the world in a different way. We worry about thinking because we care about what we and other people think. Even the most far-fetched ideas have an effect on the world. Non-Euclidean geometry and symbolic logic are about as abstract as thinking can get, but you can't understand Einsteinian gravity without the first and run computers without the second. Thinking is important to us, to others, and to the world we live in. This is one reason why we are so afraid of it: it shakes us to the core.
